findings.evidence: Lines 208–219 provide forward and inverse generator rules, so consumers need not unfold the definition.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]`; keep the body opaque and state the generator lemma as `:= (rfl)` if needed to capture definitional equality locally.
findings.issue: `quotientJacobsonMulOppositeRingEquiv` is `@[expose]` even though its public behavior is fully characterized by the two following `@[simp]` lemmas, allowing downstream proofs to depend on the first-isomorphism-theorem implementation.

findings.evidence: Repository grep finds `isUnit_one_add_mul_swap` only at lines 36 and 50, and `mem_jacobson_iff_exists_mul_eq_one` only at lines 69 and 81.
findings.fix: Make both implementation helpers `private`, leaving `isUnit_one_add_mul_comm` and the unit-valued Jacobson characterizations as the public API.
findings.issue: `isUnit_one_add_mul_swap` is publicly exposed although its result is exactly the forward implication of the public iff at line 49 and it is only used to construct that iff; similarly, `mem_jacobson_iff_exists_mul_eq_one` at MulOpposite.lean:69 is only an intermediate restatement used at line 81.

summary: The quotient equivalence unnecessarily exposes its implementation, and two proof-only directional/restatement helpers enlarge the public API without adding usable functionality.
